Q: can I use a list comprehension to write multiples of 3 within a range using addition? A:

you have to compare value%3 with 1 (not 0) to get the same values as range(1, 31, 3)

Q: What are the semantics of a+ mode in standard fopen()? A:

Is an implementation permitted to start reading too at the end of the file?

Yes.

From fopen(3) — manual page:

a+ ...
POSIX is silent on what the initial read position is when using this mode. For glibc, the initial file position for reading is at the beginning of the file, but for Android/BSD/MacOS, the initial file position for reading is at the end of the file.

(emphasis is mine)

Not only that reading from the start is not mandatory, there are systems which document that the initial position is at the end.
Cygwin is not mentioned, but it looks like it is a valid choice.

Therefore using fseek (like you did) is the correct approach.

Q: Linux Basics for Hackers : Is it a good book to start learning Hacking and Linux? A:

You have to become good programmer before start hacking. For that reason, first start with learning CPU architecture, assembly language, C, different OS.

Q: What's the industry-standard way to, with a formula, fill a range with a specific value? A:

the simplest/best way with the shortest formula

=sort("Apple"&left(A1:A5;))

The formula will only work as long cells A1:A5 don't contain error values. To handle cells that contain errors, use switch(iferror()):

=switch(iferror(A1:A5);µ;;"Apple")

Q: Query across three tables with joins A:

Straight ahead this can be done with an exists subquery:

SELECT * FORM Orders o 
WHERE exists (SELECT 1 FROM ProductSizesOptions p
                       JOIN CustomerProductSizesOptions c ON p.ProductOptionSizeID = c.ProductOptionSizeID
                       WHERE c.OrderID = o.OrderID and p.ProductOptionID = 1627)

So you get each Order once if there is any suitable CustomerProductSizesOptions-entry.

Q: CannotPullContainerError: ref pull has been retried 1 time(s): failed to copy: httpReadSeeker: failed open with 403 error A:

The failure happens because ECR image layers are downloaded from S3, and the setup only had ECR VPC endpoints (ecr.api, ecr.dkr) but no S3 access.

In private subnets (no NAT), this causes:

CannotPullContainerError: ref pull has been retried...

When pulling images from Amazon ECR, ECS:

  1. Calls ECR APIs (ecr.api, ecr.dkr)

  2. Downloads image layers from an Amazon-managed S3 bucket:

    arn:aws:s3:::prod-region-starport-layer-bucket/*

VPC Endpoints:

  • Interface endpoints

    • com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.api

    • com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.dkr

  • Gateway endpoint

    • com.amazonaws.<region>.s3 ✅ mandatory

IAM Permissions Required:

{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": [
    "ecr:GetAuthorizationToken",
    "ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability",
    "ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer",
    "ecr:BatchGetImage"
  ],
  "Resource": "*"
}

{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": "s3:GetObject",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::prod-region-starport-layer-bucket/*"
}

This S3 bucket is where ECR stores image layers.

AWS Reference Document - https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/vpc-endpoints.html
